newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: EU talks to Denmark, delays anti-Cuba trade vote.
newsitem.headline: EU talks to Denmark, delays anti-Cuba trade vote.

text.p: European Union foreign ministers on Monday delayed voting on measures to counter U.S. anti-Cuba trade laws to give themselves time to win over dissenting member-state Denmark, diplomats said.
Denmark has said it will veto the proposed measures aimed at countering Washington's Helms-Burton Act because it believes part of the EU treaty they come under compromises national sovereignty.
Foreign ministers were due to vote on the response to the Helms-Burton Act -- an amalgamation of years of U.S. anti-Cuba policy -- when they met in Luxembourg on Monday.
But an immediate vote was put off until fresh talks between Denmark, the European Commission and Ireland, the current EU president later in the day, diplomast said.
Diplomats said a vote on the measures would now probably take place on Monday evening, unless a compromise was worked out sooner.
Officials are looking to see if the reprisal measures can be passed using another section of the EU's treaty which might provide Denmark with a way out.
But diplomats say while this would have the same effect in protecting European interests, they fear the political message they wanted to send to Washington would be diluted.
Danish foreign minister Niels Helveg Petersen, arriving for Monday's meeting, said Copenhagen's "legal problems" remained over ways to counter the Act.
"We have not come to block the proposals," Petersen said. "We come to seek a solution ... but we cannot agree with it in this form."
The Danish government is currently embroiled in a court case brought by a citizens' group that accuses it of handing too much sovereignty to the EU.
